headline: Android release path for Kam na mši, built as the Flywheel reference. A signed AAB builds on every run and uploads itself to the Play internal testing track once Pavol's two secrets exist. The listing (cs-CZ + en-US) lives in the repo, with generated graphics and limits checked in tests. Pavol's part is 10 short console/one-command steps in docs/ANDROID-RELEASE.md. No account, secret, submission or payment was touched.

shipped.title: Android release path: internal-track upload via fastlane supply, listing in repo, owner steps
shipped.live_checked: Release Android was run on the branch with no secrets set, three times. Run 41788619673 (the first Release Android run ever) failed: an empty ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PATH broke Gradle with 'Cannot convert '' to File'. That was a pre-existing bug that only an unsigned release run could hit, now fixed in android/app/build.gradle. Run 41788818798 (the fix) and run 41789375821 (the review fixes) both passed end to end: build, read-back, listing check, and Play upload skipped with its notice. CI test + android are green. Two independent reviews: the first found 2 blocking problems (the listing push would fail before launch; 'Zdarma' in the short description), both fixed; the re-review found nothing blocking.

automated: Web build → cap sync → signed AAB + APK. versionCode = 100 + run number. versionName comes from the tag or the run's input.
Read-back of versionName, permissions, signature and 16 KB page-size alignment. Today there's no native code, so alignment is met.

Upload to the Play INTERNAL testing track with fastlane supply 2.241.2, with release notes (cs-CZ, en-US). If Play says the app is still a draft, it retries as a draft release and says so. No step can reach another track.
Store listing text, icon, feature graphic and screenshots from store-assets/android/metadata/, sent with that run's internal upload, only when run with upload_listing.

scripts/play-listing.mjs checks Play's limits in npm test and before upload: title 30, short 80, full 4000 characters; no price or ranking words in the title or short description; icon 512²; feature graphic 1024×500; 2–8 screenshots, 16:9–9:16, 320–3840 px.
Graphics are generated by script: scripts/play-graphics.mjs for the icon and feature graphic, and e2e/store-shots.spec.ts for the phone screenshots. All were regenerated on 4 Nov.

scripts/android-keystore.sh: one command makes the upload key and sets 4 GitHub secrets via gh. It never prints a value, and the password goes to the macOS Keychain. --play-json sets the Play service-account secret the same way.
Without secrets, the steps that need them are skipped with a notice. The build still runs.
In-app privacy link in the footer, which Play requires. The privacy policy now names iOS/Android, the in-app events and the OpenStreetMap tiles.
pavol_steps_verbatim:
## Steps

1. **Check which rules apply to your account.** Play Console → ⚙ *Settings* → *Developer
   account* → *Account details*: note **Account type** (Personal / Organization) and the
   creation date. If it is *Personal* and created after 13 Nov 2023, step 8 applies (closed
   test). Confirmation later: in the app's menu, *Test and release → Production* is locked
   and the *Dashboard* shows "Apply for production".
2. **Upload key + GitHub secrets — one command at the mini**, in your bohosluzby
   checkout (needs `gh auth login` once and a JDK):
   ```
   git pull && scripts/android-keystore.sh
   ```
   It sets the 4 `ANDROID_*` secrets and keeps the password in your macOS Keychain
   ("kam-na-msi android upload key"). Nothing secret is printed.
3. **First build:** GitHub → *Actions* → *Release Android* → *Run workflow* → branch
   `main`, version `1.5.0` → *Run*. When it is green, open the run and download the
   artifact `kam-na-msi-android-1.5.0` (the `.aab` inside).
4. **Create the app and upload that first build by hand** (Google's API can't do the very
   first upload). Play Console → *Create app* → name `Kam na mši – katolické mše`, default
   language *Czech – cs-CZ*, *App*, *Free*, tick the declarations → *Create app*.
   Then *Test and release → Testing → Internal testing* → *Create new release* → accept
   Google-generated app signing → upload the `.aab` → *Next* → *Save and publish*.
   *Testers* tab → create an e-mail list with your own Google account → *Save*.
5. **Let CI upload from now on** (one time, ~5 min):
   1. console.cloud.google.com → new project `kam-na-msi-play` → *APIs & Services* →
      enable **Google Play Android Developer API**.
   2. *IAM & Admin → Service accounts* → *Create* `play-upload` → *Done* → open it →
      *Keys → Add key → JSON* (a file downloads).
   3. Play Console → *Users and permissions* → *Invite new users* → paste the service
      account's e-mail → *App permissions* → Kam na mši → tick **Release apps to testing
      tracks** and **Manage store presence** → *Invite user*.
   4. At the mini: `scripts/android-keystore.sh --play-json ~/Downloads/<the-file>.json`,
      then delete the file.

   A newly invited service account can take up to a day before Google stops answering
   "caller does not have permission"; the next run after that works. If the Cloud
   project sits under a Workspace organisation, its policy may block JSON keys — use a
   project under your personal account.

   From now on every *Release Android* run (or tag `android-vX.Y.Z`) uploads to the
   internal track by itself.
6. **App content** — Play Console → *Policy and programs → App content*, paste from
   `docs/store/play-metadata.md`: privacy policy `https://bohosluzby.dravec.org/privacy/`,
   ads *No*, app access *all functionality without special access*, content rating
   (IARC, all *No*), target audience *18+*, Data safety (the table), news *No*,
   government *No*, financial features *none*, health *none*.
   Also *Store settings*: category *Lifestyle*, contact e-mail, website.
7. **Approve the listing text** — read `store-assets/android/metadata/cs-CZ/*.txt` and
   `en-US/*.txt` and the privacy page (updated 4 Nov). If they're right: *Actions →
   Release Android → Run workflow* with **upload_listing** ticked; it builds and uploads a
   new internal build and, with it, puts text, icon, feature graphic and screenshots on
   the listing (Play attaches listing changes to a release).
8. **Only if step 1 said so — closed test, 12 testers, 14 days.** *Testing → Closed
   testing* → *Create track* → *Promote release* from internal → *Testers*: an e-mail list
   (or Google Group) with at least 12 people → *Save* → send them the opt-in link. They opt
   in and keep the app installed for 14 days in a row. Then *Dashboard → Apply for
   production* (Google answers in about 7 days). New personal accounts also verify a
   phone: the *Dashboard* task, in the Play Console app on an Android 10+ phone.
9. **Trader status** (all accounts, by 1 Feb 2027): Play Console → *Settings* →
   *Developer account* → declare trader / non-trader (a free app with no income: non-trader).
10. **Production** — *Testing → Internal (or Closed) testing* → the release → *Promote
   release → Production* → *Review* → *Start rollout to production*. This is the only
   submit; CI never does it.

research.file: docs/research/2026-11-04-google-play.md (one section per topic, with source URL and page date for each finding)
findings: Target API 36 (Android 16) is required for new apps and updates since 31 Aug 2026. Existing apps need ≥35 to stay visible. No later deadline is announced (API 37 in Aug 2027 is an inference). The app targets 36. Sources: https://developer.android.com/google/play/requirements/target-sdk (updated 2026-10-28), https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/11926878

AAB is required for new apps, and Play App Signing is required with AAB. Ours is only the upload key, which Pavol can reset in Play Console. New apps are auto-enrolled in Google-generated quantum-ready hybrid signing. Sources: https://developer.android.com/guide/app-bundle (2026-06-24), https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/9842756

Play Developer API: linking a Cloud project is no longer required. Create a GCP project, enable the API, create a service account and key, then invite its email in Play Console → Users and permissions. 'Release apps to testing tracks' is enough for internal; 'Manage store presence' covers the listing. Sources: https://developers.google.com/android-publisher/getting_started (2025-12-18), https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/9844686

The first upload must go through Play Console. The API only works on an app with at least one upload, and it can't fill legal consents. Sources: https://developers.google.com/android-publisher/edits (2025-12-18), https://docs.fastlane.tools/actions/supply/, fastlane/fastlane#14686
Draft apps accept only draft releases through the API. This comes from third-party reports, not Google's docs; the workflow handles both outcomes.

Listing limits: name 30, short 80, full 4,000 characters. Graphics: icon 512×512 32-bit PNG ≤1 MB; feature graphic 1024×500; screenshots 2–8 per device type, sides 320–3840 px, long side ≤2× the short side. Tablet screenshots are optional. Sources: https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/9859152, https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/9866151

App content: Data safety is required for closed, open and production tracks, not internal-only. Location used only on the device is not 'collected'. A privacy policy is needed both in the listing and inside the app. Ads, target audience (avoid under-13), content rating (IARC), and the health, financial, government and news declarations all apply. Sources: https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/10787469, https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/9859455

Personal accounts created after 13 Nov 2023 must run a closed test with ≥12 testers opted in for 14 continuous days, then use Apply for production (about 7 days). Organisation accounts are presumably exempt, though the page doesn't say so outright. New personal accounts also verify an Android 10+ device in the Play Console app. Sources: https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/14151465, https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/14316361

16 KB page size: updates without it are blocked from 1 Feb 2027. Java/Kotlin-only apps comply, and the workflow now checks. Source: https://developer.android.com/guide/practices/page-sizes (2026-10-16)

Android developer verification since 30 Sep 2026 (BR/ID/SG/TH, global in 2027): Play apps are registered automatically, so it doesn't block Play, but it affects the sideloaded GitHub .apk. EEA/UK trader declaration is due by 1 Feb 2027. Sources: https://developer.android.com/developer-verification/guides (2026-08-18), https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/13628312
research.closed_test_check: Play Console → ⚙ Settings → Developer account → Account details: Account type (Personal/Organization) and creation date. Personal and created after 13 Nov 2023 means the closed test applies. Confirmation: Test and release → Production is locked and the Dashboard shows 'Apply for production'. The label was read from help pages, not a live Console.

data_safety_from_code: docs/store/play-metadata.md § Data safety. flywheel-client.ts sends events (event name, props, random visitor_id/session_id, time) and optional feedback (score, Sean Ellis answer, free text) to Supabase over https. Props carry filters, day, church ids, a town picked by hand, and timings. Coordinates are never sent: distances are computed on the device. No accounts, ads SDK or advertising ID. Declared as: App interactions (required), Other user-generated content (optional), Crash logs/Diagnostics, and Device or other IDs, all for Analytics and not shared. Location: not collected.
privacy_policy: https://bohosluzby.dravec.org/privacy/ exists in Czech and English. It now names the iOS and Android apps, lists the in-app events accurately, and mentions OpenStreetMap tiles. It's linked from the app footer (new). The wording changed, so approving it is part of step 7.

decisions.why: The brief says so, and promotion is Pavol's step in the Console.

decisions.question: How the listing reaches Play
options: with the internal upload when upload_listing is ticked
decisions.why: Before launch, a listing-only call looks for the production track and fails (review finding, checked in supply's source).

decisions.default_taken: 1.5.0, given as the run input in step 3
decisions.why: It's the same feature set as iOS 1.5.

decisions.question: Short description 'Zdarma'
decisions.default_taken: dropped; the checker rejects price/ranking words
decisions.why: Play's metadata policy. 'Zdarma, bez reklam' stays in the full description.

decisions.question: Data safety: a town picked by hand
decisions.why: It isn't the device's location. The fallback answer is in ANDROID-RELEASE.md.

decisions.question: Target audience
decisions.why: It stays out of the Families policy. The app is suitable for all ages but isn't designed for children.

uncertain:
## Uncertain

- Whether step 8 applies: depends on your account (step 1).
- Draft-app error text and behaviour come from third-party reports, not Google's docs —
  the workflow handles both outcomes.
- Data safety: a town picked by hand travels in an analytics event. Drafted as an app
  interaction, not *Location* (it isn't the device's location). If Google disagrees, add
  *Approximate location* · collected · analytics.
- The footer's *Podpořit* link (GitHub Sponsors) is fine on iOS 1.4. Play's payments
  policy limits donation links for non-charities; if review objects, hide it on Android.
- The exact Console label for the account type (step 1) was read from Google's help
  pages, not a live Console.
- The icon is an RGB PNG without alpha; Play's spec says 32-bit PNG. Play usually accepts
  it; if the listing upload complains, re-export with alpha in `scripts/play-graphics.mjs`.
- The first CI upload sends release notes in cs-CZ and en-US while en-US is not yet a
  listing language; if Play refuses, run step 7 first (it adds en-US).
